STEP 1 - Scene: A tray meal (airline/institutional style) with a plate of stir-fried noodles with meat pieces, a smaller plate of sliced white meat (likely turkey or chicken), a chocolate bar, a cup of juice, a cup of water, and a plastic-wrapped utensil. Photographed from a fairly high, near-overhead angle. The number card 3098 and color chart are photo-lab markers, not food.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The noodle plate is about 22 cm across (undistorted width), so area ≈ 3.14 × (11)² ≈ 380 cm². The sliced meat plate is about 16 cm across, area ≈ 3.14 × (8)² ≈ 200 cm². I'll treat the noodle plate as the main vessel for percentages.

STEP 3 - Items: (a) stir-fried noodles, (b) braised/fried meat chunks mixed into noodles, (c) sliced cooked white meat on a separate plate. Chocolate bar, juice and water are not weighed as plated food here; they are listed separately only if needed. I'll estimate the noodles and meats.

STEP 4 - Area: Noodles cover about 75% of the 380 cm² plate (≈285 cm²). Meat chunks cover about 20% of that plate (≈75 cm²), overlapping the noodle surface. Sliced meat covers about 85% of its 200 cm² plate (≈170 cm²).

STEP 5 - Volume: Noodles: 285 cm² × 2.5 cm ≈ 710 ml (outer envelope). Meat chunks: 75 cm² × 1.2 cm ≈ 90 ml. Sliced meat: 170 cm² × 0.8 cm ≈ 135 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Noodles 710 ml × 0.8 ≈ 570 g... this is too high for a visible portion with gaps; the noodle pile is loose and thin, so I apply the bulk density to a shallower effective height (≈1.5 cm, giving ≈430 ml) → ≈340 g. Meat chunks 90 ml × 0.95 ≈ 85 g. Sliced meat 135 ml × 0.95 ≈ 130 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Stir-fried noodles (cooked, with oil) ≈ 160 kcal/100 g → 340 g × 1.6 = 544 kcal. Braised meat chunks (pork/chicken, fried) ≈ 220 kcal/100 g → 85 g × 2.2 = 187 kcal. Sliced cooked turkey/chicken breast ≈ 135 kcal/100 g → 130 g × 1.35 = 176 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A full tray noodle plate plus a generous meat portion totaling about 555 g and roughly 900 kcal is plausible for a hearty airline or hospital meal. The chocolate bar, juice and water are excluded from this estimate.
